details:
**Coat of many colors**
The richly ornamented coat that Jacob gave to Joseph, his favorite son, in Genesis 37. It made his brothers jealous, and they later dipped it in goat's blood to convince Jacob that Joseph had been killed by a wild animal.

**Potiphar's wife**
As a slave in Egypt, Joseph served Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, whose wife (traditionally named Zuleika or Zulaikha) tried to seduce him. When he refused, she falsely accused him of trying to rape her, and he was thrown into prison.

**Pharaoh's dreams of fat and lean cows**
Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dreams, in which seven thin cows ate seven fat cows and seven thin ears of grain swallowed seven full ones. He explained that they meant seven years of plenty would be followed by seven years of famine, and he advised storing grain during the good years.

**Grand vizier of Egypt**
As a reward for interpreting Pharaoh's dreams, Joseph was made the second most powerful man in Egypt, in charge of preparing for the famine. Pharaoh gave him the Egyptian name Zaphnath-Paaneah and the wife Asenath.

**Sold into slavery by his brothers**
Joseph's jealous brothers threw him into a pit (well) and sold him to traders, who took him to Egypt as a slave. Reuben, the eldest, tried to save him, and Judah suggested selling him instead of killing him.

**Cupbearer and baker**
While in prison, Joseph interpreted the dreams of two of Pharaoh's officials. He correctly predicted that the cupbearer would be restored to his post and the baker executed, and the cupbearer later remembered him when Pharaoh needed a dream interpreter.

**Silver cup in Benjamin's sack**
When his brothers came to Egypt to buy grain during the famine, Joseph, who they did not recognize, had his silver cup hidden in the sack of his youngest brother Benjamin and then accused Benjamin of theft. This tested whether the brothers had changed before Joseph revealed who he was and brought the family to Egypt.

**Dream of the sheaves**
In his youth, Joseph dreamed that his sheaf of grain stood upright while his brothers' sheaves bowed down to it. In a second dream, the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowed to him, which angered his brothers even more.

**Manasseh and Ephraim**
Joseph's two sons by Asenath. When the aged and nearly blind Jacob blessed them, he crossed his hands to put his right hand on the younger Ephraim, giving him the greater blessing. Both became founders of tribes of Israel.

**Rachel, Jacob, and Laban**
Joseph was the first son of Rachel, Jacob's beloved wife. Jacob worked fourteen years for Rachel's father Laban to marry her and her sister Leah, and Rachel later died giving birth to Joseph's younger brother Benjamin.

**Burial at Shechem**
Before dying, Joseph made the Israelites swear to carry his bones out of Egypt. During the Exodus, Moses took his remains, and they were buried at Shechem in the land of Canaan.

**Joseph, husband of Mary**
In the New Testament, Joseph is the carpenter husband of Mary and the earthly father of Jesus. The genealogies in Matthew and Luke disagree on whether his father was Jacob or Heli.

**Joseph's dreams in Matthew**
When Joseph learned Mary was pregnant, he planned to divorce her quietly until an angel told him in a dream not to be afraid to take her as his wife. In a later dream, an angel told him to "flee to Egypt" with Mary and the infant Jesus to escape Herod, and after Herod's death he settled the family in Nazareth.

**Feasts of Saint Joseph**
The Catholic Church celebrates Saint Joseph's main feast on March 19. In 1955, Pope Pius XII created the feast of Saint Joseph the Worker on May 1 as a Christian alternative to the socialist May Day.
